issues.sym: The car won't start or power up after you unlock it, a dead-battery symbol or a 12V charging warning appears, or it stalls or limits power while driving. Some owners have been towed several times.
issues.why: The small 12-volt battery that runs the car's computers drains or isn't kept charged properly. Software, the start/stop system and battery-monitoring faults all play a part, and Volvo has issued several service bulletins on 12V charging messages.
issues.next: Have the 12V battery and charging system tested and ask the dealer about current software and bulletins. Keep records of each failure; repeat cases may qualify under lemon laws.

issues.t: Rearview camera image may not appear (recall)
issues.sym: The screen shows a blank image or 'Camera is temporarily not available' when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: A software fault in the infotainment system stops the backup camera image from showing. Volvo recalled 2021-2025 XC40s twice (25V-282, then 25V-908) because the first fix wasn't enough.
issues.next: Look behind you and use mirrors when reversing. Check your VIN for open recalls; the fix is a free software update, often over the air.

issues.sym: The electric XC40 suddenly loses drive power or shuts down completely while driving; doors may not unlock afterward and it may need a tow.
issues.why: The battery energy control module could reset and disconnect the high-voltage system. Volvo recalled 2021-2022 XC40 Recharge models for a software fix.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for open recalls. If it still happens after the update, report it to the dealer and NHTSA.

issues.t: Water can corrode the accelerator pedal sensor (recall)
issues.sym: The accelerator responds erratically or not at all, or the car loses drive power.
issues.why: Water can get into a wiring harness and corrode the accelerator pedal sensor circuit on 2021-2022 XC40 Recharge models.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer inspects the wiring, adds a splice and replaces parts as needed for free.

issues.t: Brakes may not work in One Pedal Drive (recall)
issues.sym: While coasting down a hill using One Pedal Drive, braking can be reduced or lost.
issues.why: A brake module software fault affected 2023-2024 XC40 electric models and 2025 EX40s (recall 25V-392).
issues.next: Don't use One Pedal Drive until the free brake software update is installed. Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking may fail or brake on its own (recall)
issues.sym: The automatic emergency braking may not stop for an obstacle, or the car brakes hard for no reason.
issues.why: A software and hardware mismatch kept the collision avoidance system from detecting objects properly. Volvo recalled 2019-2020 XC40s for a software update.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free update done.

issues.t: Infotainment screen freezes, reboots or loses sound
issues.sym: The center screen freezes, goes black or reboots, apps stop working, profiles reset, or the audio cuts out, sometimes taking safety chimes with it.
issues.why: Software faults in the infotainment unit are common across XC40 years. Volvo has issued bulletins for touch-screen and audio problems.
issues.next: Restart the system by holding the home button, keep software up to date, and report repeat failures to the dealer.

issues.t: Check engine light with no clear cause
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on and returns soon after being cleared, with no obvious drivability problem.
issues.why: Software and module faults can set warning codes on these cars. Volvo has issued bulletins for some check engine light codes.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer to check for related bulletins or software updates.

issues.sym: ABS, stability control or brake warning lights come on and the pedal may feel stiff.
issues.why: A diagnostic error in a brake control module could switch off brake support functions such as ABS and stability control on 2023 models.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN for open recalls; Volvo provides a free software update.

issues.sym: The car brakes or warns of a collision at highway speed with nothing in the way.
issues.why: The forward collision avoidance system can misread the road ahead.
issues.next: Keep the windshield camera and radar area clean and report each event to the dealer and NHTSA.

issues.t: Left rear turn signal may not work (recall)
issues.sym: The left rear turn signal doesn't flash.
issues.why: A software diagnostic error in the central electronic module affected about 17,000 2024 models.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the fix is a free software update.

issues.t: Shudder or reduced transmission performance warning
issues.sym: A 'transmission performance reduced' message, torque that surges or fluctuates, or shuddering when accelerating between about 40 and 65 mph.
issues.why: Volvo issued service bulletins on 2024 models for transmission control codes, torque fluctuation and shudder.
issues.next: Have the dealer check for transmission codes and apply the related bulletins or software.

issues.sym: A rattling noise from the engine area, often on startup or at low speeds.
issues.why: The turbocharger wastegate rod can rattle; Volvo issued a service bulletin for it.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about the wastegate bulletin while the car is under warranty.

issues.sym: Creaking or knocking from the front over bumps, or steering wheel vibration above 60 mph.
issues.why: Volvo issued bulletins for upper front suspension noise and steering wheel vibration on 2024 models.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect the front suspension and check for the related bulletins.

issues.t: Coolant level drops with no visible leak
issues.sym: The low coolant warning comes on and the reservoir needs topping up, but there is no puddle.
issues.why: Owners report coolant loss without an obvious external leak; a small internal or hidden leak may be the cause.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested while under warranty. Don't ignore a low coolant warning.

issues.sym: Vibration or pulsing when braking, with rotors replaced at fairly low mileage.
issues.why: Some owners needed front and rear rotors replaced within 15,000-25,000 miles because of pad material transfer and warping.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured. Avoid holding the brakes hard after heavy stops, and ask about warranty coverage on early wear.

issues.sym: The car suddenly won't start or drive because of an electrical failure, sometimes with no visible water inside.
issues.why: Water reportedly got in through seals underneath the car and damaged electrical parts.
issues.next: Check carpets and under-seat areas for dampness. If the car fails electrically, ask the dealer to inspect for water entry and keep records.

issues.sym: The airbag light or an SRS message comes on, sometimes saying airbags may not work, and may go away on its own.
issues.why: The cause wasn't confirmed; some cases were fixed by the dealer, possibly with software.
issues.next: Treat the warning seriously and have the dealer read the airbag codes.

issues.sym: Stitching on the seats splits open at low mileage.
issues.why: Seam failures on early seats.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to replace the cover under warranty if it is still covered.

issues.sym: Messages saying parking sensors are blocked, or false parking alerts, even when the sensors look clean.
issues.why: The parking sensors are sensitive to dirt, ice and alignment, and some early cars gave false warnings.
issues.next: Clean the sensors and check for paint or bumper damage. Have the dealer test them if warnings continue.

issues.t: Emergency call may not send location (recall)
issues.sym: No obvious symptom; after a crash the car's emergency call may not send its GPS location.
issues.why: A fault in the emergency call system on early 2019 models.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the fix is free.

issues.t: Emergency call warning may hide a real fault (recall)
issues.sym: A false warning message about the emergency call system.
issues.why: A software issue could show a false warning that hides a real eCall failure on a small number of 2023 models.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; a free software update fixes it.

issues.sym: The brake pedal moves or feels loose.
issues.why: On a small number of early 2019 cars the brake pedal may not have been riveted correctly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If your car is included, don't drive it until the pedal is inspected.

issues.sym: The rear seatback may fold forward in hard braking.
issues.why: Rear seatback lock strikers were missing on a few early 2019 cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the fix is free.

issues.t: Seat belt may not hold a child seat tight (recall)
issues.sym: A child seat won't stay tight after the belt is pulled out to lock it.
issues.why: The seat belt's automatic locking retractor could release too early.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; dealers inspect and replace belts as needed.
